title: Choose Shortlist's visual world
question: The roll assigned Galley Proof. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Galley Proof
options.lineage: typesetters' galley proofs and BS 5261 proofreading marks
options.thesis: The machine sets the resume as a galley proof; every check is a proof mark in the margin.
options.viewport: The original (the manuscript) beside one long machine-set galley of the record, with a ruled proof margin where flags and the computed experience tally are marked.
options.risk: Turns bookish if set in a serif on cream; it must stay on cool galley stock with a grotesque text face.

raised.raise: No radius anywhere; every rule and mark drawn at one device pixel in three ink values plus the two proof colours.
Missing details stay printed as empty ruled slots carrying their proof mark, never silently omitted.
Proof red is reserved for what the recruiter must check and appears nowhere else.

options.label: Application Form
options.lineage: official application forms with a For Office Use Only column
options.thesis: The record is a filled-in official form, and the code's checks tick the office-use-only column.
options.viewport: Numbered boxed fields beside the original, with a shaded office-use-only column where each check is ticked or stamped.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of HR paperwork; it can feel bureaucratic and dense.

options.label: Coupon Wallet
options.thesis: Each section is a carbon-copy coupon; checks stamp themselves on the coupon and nothing disappears.
options.viewport: Contact, career and skills as tabbed coupons beside the original, missing details stamped NOT GIVEN.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and states missing data most plainly; recruiters do not identify with air travel.
options.risk: Reads as travel novelty if the stamps turn decorative.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.thesis: Original and record set as twin columns around a rail of keys linking each source line to its field.
options.viewport: Original left, record right, a centre rail of keys joining them, flags hanging in the outer margin.
options.case: Strongest verification mechanism; a scholarly edition is far from a recruiter's world.
options.risk: Scholarly and slow for a fast screening pass.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Fields as rows of flaps that cascade into place.
options.viewport: A board of candidate fields flipping into place.
options.case: Fuses poorly: per-character flipping is a gimmick for a recruiter.
options.kept: Columns never move; only their contents change.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: One neutral scale and a single rationed accent.
options.viewport: Claim-and-proof panels in a neutral grid.
options.case: This is the generic SaaS look you ruled out.
options.kept: The accent is rationed to a handful of uses.

options.label: Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Each candidate as a cast member with fixed personal furniture.
options.viewport: A candidate card with a name plate and fixed fields.
options.case: Playful; you ruled that out for HR.
options.kept: Every record carries the same fixed slots in the same order.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: The career as a course run control to control over a map of years.
options.viewport: Jobs as numbered legs over a terrain of years.
options.case: Vivid for the timeline, but recruiters do not read maps.
options.kept: One colour is reserved for the single concern that needs attention.

canonCard.label: The ATS standard
canonCard.thesis: The applicant-tracking dashboard: candidate card, avatar, skill pills, done at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Candidate card on top, sections in cards below, original in a side drawer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every ATS by design.
